support_contract.description: A space’s support fees in USD cents, included minutes per calendar month, direct channels, dates and the person supplying support.

support_contract_pending.description: An admin’s support contract terms waiting for the payment provider to accept them.

support_contract_billing.description: The subscription, one-time invoice and any connected account that owns those Stripe objects.

support_contract_time.description: Minutes of work on one space’s support contract, dated and described by the person recording it.

release_view.description: Serving settings and a compressed Files index for the live source.

app_icon.description: The platform artwork requested and drawn for an app.

app_icon_draw.description: Draw an icon for a released app without artwork of its own.

app_splash.description: The splash images drawn for an app, by the key of the set its pages name (@yaks/platform/splash): its icon on its background, for every iPhone and iPad screen, dark too where the app has a dark background. requested asks for the set again.

app_splash_draw.description: Draw a released app's splash images from its icon and background.

person_name.description: Where a person's doc{title} came from.

sessions_ended.description: All browser credentials issued before session rows were ended.

browser_session.description: One signed-in browser, ended by cancelling its row.

place.$comment: Where its network placed it when it signed in or last renewed.

located.description: Where one source puts one of a person's places, roughly: home, work, current (where they are now) or a place they named, as their own words (said), their billing address (billing) or their connection (network) put it. One row per person, place and source; never a street address or coordinates.

kind.description: home, work, current, or the name they gave a place

region.description: its state or province as a code, such as MI

country.description: its two-letter country code, such as US

zone.description: its IANA time zone, such as America/Detroit

area.description: a three-digit telephone area code, such as 269

located.$comment: Where one source puts one of a person's places, roughly (@yaks/platform/located): their home, their work, where they are now or a place they named, as their own words, their billing address or their connection said it. Their phone's area code is read off their `phone{number}` instead, so it is never kept twice. Never a street or coordinates; read only for the person and their own Operator.

cli_grant.description: One CLI grant, revoked by cancelling its row.
cli_grant.$comment: One CLI grant (workers/yak/grants.ts): whose it is, its id, the space it is narrowed to, and when it dies. Revoked by cancelling its row.

standing_link.description: One standing sign-in link, revoked by cancelling its row.
standing_link.$comment: One standing sign-in link (workers/yak/link.ts), revoked the same way.

binding.$comment: Storage survives config edits and renames. Only the kernel may record account resource ids, so an app cannot claim another tenant's data.

former.$comment:
Every address an app has answered at, oldest first: `slug` the one it was born at, `slugs` each one a rename left behind. Address history and nothing else — its storage handle is @yaks/platform’s `app.store`, which is why a rename moves an address and never a byte (T-34657). Bare slugs, in the space's own namespace, so a space rename leaves every app's history standing.

It was named `alias` until T-34390, when that word became the platform's own (@yaks/alias, in {@link coreDocs}): a name any entity may wear in any store. Two things cannot share one word, and the one every store speaks wins — so the app's addresses are `former`, which is what the record is about.

A space wears it too, for the same reason and in the same shape (T-34658): its birth subdomain and every one a rename left behind, each still redirecting. Not unique here — uniqueness is over an address within a space for an app, and over the whole platform for a space, and neither is one property's own race; the tools decide both (tools.ts `taken`).

home.$comment:
Which app is the space's front page, and the paths its worker sees first before the app whose slug owns them (D-34197, T-34227). One fact, one place: the app wearing `home` is the home app, and its globs are properties of the same word — a `space.home` beside it would be a second place to say the same thing, and two copies of one fact drift.

At most one app per space wears it. The vocabulary cannot say so — `unique` covers one component's own properties and `home` has no space of its own — so it is the directory's rule instead (directory.ts `homing`, where moving it is one batch that drops the old and adds the new).

A property is a scalar (@yaks/vocab `storable`), so the list is JSON in one text property — ordered, and read back by router.ts `firstOf`. The `former.slugs` above splits on whitespace instead, which is the older form of a list here; JSON is the one that round-trips exactly what an agent passed.

own.$comment: The space is the person's own: the one minted for them, which their settings and an unnamed tool call mean (directory.ts `own`). A rename leaves it standing, where their address no longer names it.

build.description: May edit and release the files of this app.

grant.$comment: A seat reaches every app in its space; this reaches one (T-37615). It is the word @yaks/member already uses for that — the same three levels, the same meaning — said here because the ladder a page is read by is the platform's roster and this is its other rung: somebody invited to one app holds that app's data and its page as a member does, and holds no other app in the space at all. Never its files: writing an app's bytes stays a member's act (apps.ts, public/docs/sharing.md).

app_transfer.description: An owner offers an app to another person in the space they own.

app_transfer_answer.description: The recipient’s answer to an app transfer, with the addresses left behind on acceptance.

domain_transfer.description: An owner offers a domain to the owners of another space.

domain_transfer_answer.description: An owner’s answer to a domain transfer, or withdrawal when another space accepted.

operator_reach.$comment: Another space's Operator let into this one (T-136179): the Operator of `operator` works in `space` with `role`, for whoever may ask it there. A space's owner writes it on its People page (operator-reach.ts), and `by` is who.

space_logo.description: The space's logo: the SHA-256 of its image's bytes and their type.
space_logo.$comment: The picture a space wears where its first letter stood (pages.ts `choice`): the bytes at `sha` in the bucket under the space's handle (apps.ts `LOGO`), and their image type. Its owner sets it in the space's settings, or takes it off.

byline.description: A paid space's choice to show "Website by yaks.app" at the foot of its apps' pages.
byline.$comment: A paid space's choice to sign its apps' pages "Website by yaks.app" at their foot (@yaks/platform/woven `badged`, public/badge.js), linking to yaks.app's page for organizations. Its owner turns it on in the space's settings, or with space_set; off where it is not worn. A space on the free plan wears the badge instead.

invite.$comment: A seat or a grant offered and not yet taken (invite.ts, T-37880). `to` is the space (a seat) or the app (a grant), one property the way `hostname.serves` is, and accepting is one batch that writes the `member` or `grant` row and drops this one. A word of its own rather than a pending mark on the seat, so everything that reads `member` and `grant` (reach, the roster, a bare app slug) reads accepted rows and nothing else, with no filter for a new reader to forget. `sent` is when its latest letter went, which is what its inviter asks when the person says they cannot get in (people.ts), and `by` who sent it, which is who the letter's link names to whoever opens it (pages.ts `invited`).

inviting.$comment: How many invitations this person has sent in the hour it names (invite.ts `CAP`). On the inviter's own row, because the cap is theirs and an invitation row dies when it is accepted or withdrawn, which would hand a sender back the letter it had counted.

operator_alerts.$comment: How a person is told what their Operators tell them away from the page (operator-alerts.ts): on the browsers they allowed, by text, by email, or only in their Updates. Without it, by text when they agreed to texts, else by email. `declined` is when they answered Not now to alerts on a device offered in the conversation, which is then not offered again; their settings still turn alerts on.

free_spaces.$comment: How many free spaces this person may own, on their own row, where the platform raised it for them (admin_spaces, plans.ts `freeSpaces`): a null `count` is no limit, and a person without one gets `SPACES`.

role_free_spaces.$comment: How many free spaces a seat of each role in the platform's own space may own, on that space's row (admin_spaces with a role, plans.ts `freeSpaces`): each role a `free_spaces`, beneath a person's own and above `SPACES`.

desk_sidebar.$comment: How a person keeps the side of their yaks.app pages (desk-pages.ts `deskFrame`, operator-page.ts `side`): collapsed to a rail of icons, or open with each one's name beside it, the way it was without it.

desk_aside.$comment: Whether a person keeps what sits at the right of their yaks.app pages (frame.ts `Aside`, the conversation's helpers and lists) put away to a rail, the page centered in the whole width; open without it.

dismissed_suggestions.$comment: What a person dismissed of the suggestions on a space's Dashboard (@yaks/platform/dashboard), each `<space eid> <feature>`: a dismissed suggestion never comes back.

mcp_list.$comment: One list an MCP server a person connected offers their Operator's page, drawn beside the conversation with no model turn (operator-lists.ts), on an entity of its own whose `doc{title}` heads it: the `server`'s `tool` called with `args` (a JSON object, read whole), whose rows are drawn in its order. `waits` says its rows wait on the person, so the bar and the installed page's icon count them; `ord` is its place among the server's lists.

mentions.$comment: Where an id the same server's rows carry (T-123) opens, on its `mcp_server` row: `url` with `{id}` where the id goes. The Operator page makes each such id in a reply a link there (operator-draw.ts `opening`).

oauth_grant.$comment: One OAuth grant a person holds, as their agents and services are listed (grant-rows.ts): written as the provider writes the grant to KV, cancelled when it deletes it, and holding none of its secrets. A token is refused once its grant's row is cancelled (asking.ts). Its eid is derived from the grant's id. Times are unix seconds; `until` is when KV lets a grant whose code was never exchanged go.

grants_listed.$comment: On a person's row: their `oauth_grant` rows are whole, every grant they held before the rows began copied in from KV since `at`.

public_file.description: A file an app published at a path of its address, served to anyone before the app runs.
public_file.$comment: A file an app published at a path of its address (public-files.ts): served to anyone there, before the app runs, whatever its access. Its eid is derived from the app and the path, so an address holds one file. The bytes are the app's, under its own prefix (`public/<sha>`).

restored.$comment:
One time this app's store, or this space's Operator (`space`), was put back to a moment (recover.ts, T-34507): when it was asked for, the moment asked for, who asked, and the bookmark the store stood at before it moved.

An entity of its own per restore, like `deploy`, and not a word on the app row — because the record exists so that a restore can itself be undone, and a second restore overwriting the first would take away the way back from it. It lives in the directory, which is a different object from the store it describes, so the trail survives the very recovery it is about: what the store held is wound back, and what happened to it is still written down here.

trashed.$comment:
That this app — or this space — is in the trash, and since when (erase.ts, T-34430, T-34431). A delete marks it and keeps everything: the bytes, the store, the slug. While it is worn the app answers nothing on the web, leaves everyone's tool and view lists, is not the front page whatever else it wears, and its mail bounces; a space wearing it does all of that for every app in it at once. `app_restore` and `space_restore` take the word off and give all of that back, and thirty days on the daily sweep erases it for good.

One word on the row rather than a state property beside it, for the reason `home` is one: what is in the trash is what wears this, and a second copy of the same fact drifts from it. That is also why an app and a space share the word — it says one thing, thrown away and since when, and every reader asks the row in front of it.

untrashed.$comment: That this app came back out of the trash, and when (erase.ts `untrash`). A restore puts it on and the next trash takes it off. It ranks the app among its space's homes (directory.ts `ranked`): a word another app took while this one was away stays that app's for the space, and this app keeps its own for its own pages and rows.

screenshot.$comment: An uploaded image the owner chose to represent this app. Its bytes and attachment live in the app's store; only the content address lives here.

theme.$comment: The colours an app's owner set for its installed chrome (apps.ts `manifesting`/`pinned`, T-33055) — settable by the app, through `app_set`, never guessed off its page: an app that names neither gets the platform's own palette instead of a browser's default grey.

seeded.$comment: That this app's store has been seeded, and by which release (seed.ts, T-34327). The mark is what makes the seed a once — a redeploy finds it and writes nothing, so the data an app comes with never lands on top of what the person has changed since. It lives on the app rather than in the store because an install mints a new app row and a new store together, and the copy is meant to be seeded again.

demo.$comment: A private published app's sample store (./visits.ts, D-134327): the handle of the store holding its published seed, which strangers read, the sha of the declaration and seed it was made from, and the version and release it was made at, which strangers are served. Server-owned: a handle an app could write is a door into another app's store.

visit.$comment: A browser's own store of an app it visited without a seat (./visits.ts, D-134327), on its `worked` edge to the app: the store's handle and where its uploads go, both written once at its first write, when it was last used (at most hourly), and the app it became when its person installed it. Server-owned for the reason `demo` is.

seller.$comment:
The connected account this space sells through (sell.ts, T-34524). Direct charges: the connected account is the merchant, so this is the whole of what the platform keeps about it — the payment provider it is held at (`via`, its name: `stripe`), the id every call names it by, and the provider's two answers about whether it is ready: `submitted`, they finished its form, and `ready`, it will take money for them. Everything else about the merchant — their bank, their business details, their disputes — is the provider's and stays there.

Server-owned, all four, for the reason `plan` is: `ready` is what the checkout door reads before it takes anybody's money, and a property a space could write for itself is a space selling before its provider ever said it may. Only the provider's webhook and `space_sell` write them, through the kernel's own door (directory.ts `stamp`).

`house` marks a space that sells on the platform's own account rather than one of its own (T-2983): the platform is the merchant and pays the provider's fees, no fee is taken, and there is no `account`. Only the platform's owner sets it, with `yak admin house`.

phone_line.$comment:
A number the platform holds for a space (numbers.ts): bought through the phone lent as `via`, on the platform's account, at the price it was bought at in dollars, `upfront` once and `monthly`, and the toll-free verification filed for it by the provider's id. What it is approved for: calls where `voice`, texts to people who know it where `sms`, and texts to many once its 10DLC `campaign` is registered, by the campaign's id (./numbers.ts `uses`). `called` is when the last call charged to the space began (workers/yak/number-upkeep.ts). Whichever space or app row wears it as `phone{number}` is where it texts from; the line says only who holds it. The row wears the wake that charges each later month (meter-graph.ts `lines`). A space's erasure leaves the line for the return job to release and bury, with the platform paying any carrier charges after erasure.

Stamped, all of it, for the reason `seller` is: it is money the platform spends, written only by the number tools (numbers.ts).

phone_login.description: An owner seat that requested a softphone sign-in for a held number.

phone_slow.description: A phone provider’s run of slow answers, reported once it lasts an hour.

phone_release.description: Carrier work to stop or permanently return a number after it or its space is deleted. Its line is the phone_line, which holds the number (phone_line.number).

fee.$comment:
What the platform takes from one sale, in basis points (sell.ts `fee`), on the platform's own space row — `yak`, the one row in this directory that is the platform rather than a customer. Unset reads as 0, which is every sale until somebody sets a rate.

Stamped, and the only writer is the owner's own door (sell.ts `fees`). A fee a space could write for itself is a seller choosing what they pay us; a fee written around that door is one the read cache would go on answering for a TTL, and the rate a sale is charged has to be the rate the owner set a moment ago.

budget.$comment: A space's monthly dollar budget for models and voice, in place of its plan's (meter.ts `limitOf`). Stamped, and written only by the platform owner's door (budget.ts), for the reason the fee is, and by a newcomer's start (newcomer.ts `oneBuild`), whose budget is one build's and says so (`newcomer`) until keeping it lifts the budget whole.

free_ai_budget.description: The Free plan’s monthly AI allowance in dollars, on the platform’s space.

starter.$comment: The dollars a space holds once, before its monthly budget, where it holds other than plans.ts `STARTER`: none on a person's later spaces (directory.ts `mint`). Stamped, for the reason the budget is.

visitor_share.$comment: The percent of a space's month budget for models and voice that its apps' visitors may spend together (meter.ts `visiting`), and the model calls one visitor may ask for in a day (meter.ts `visitorCalls`), where its owner set them with space_set; none is meter.ts `VISITORS` and `VISITOR_CALLS`. The owner's to write, so it is not stamped.

started.$comment: The space a person's starter went to (directory.ts `mint`): worn from their first space on, and kept once that space is gone, so the starter is theirs once.

subscribed.$comment: The space a person's first paid subscription went to, kept when the space is gone.

pro_grant.$comment: When a space first took the Pro plan, paid or comped, and was given plans.ts `PRO_GRANT` of building credit (billing.ts `granted`): once per space.

newcomer.$comment: When a person came in by the home page's box (newcomer.ts), before they had an address: a newcomer (directory.ts `newcomer`) until they sign in on that browser or their space is erased, when the row goes (erase.ts `vacated`). `campaign` is the one their arrival named (arrival.ts `campaign`), '' for none, which the funnel counts their steps under when no request of theirs is there to say it (directory.ts `stepper`). `client` is what kind of client opened it, as the funnel says it (@yaks/platform/visitor `classed`): `browser`, `verified`, `agent` or `bot`, or `test` for one whose arrival names an agent's check (@yaks/platform/bots `CHECK`). Only a browser's is a person's (directory.ts `testIs`): a script's, such as an agent checking the box through curl or Deno's fetch, is counted apart.

arrived.description: Where a person came from when they signed up: the door, and the page, campaign, app, assistant or inviter that brought them.
arrived.$comment: Where a person came from when they signed up (workers/yak arrivals.ts `welcomed`): written once, by the kernel, the first time they come in by any door, and never moved after. `door` is the way in: the home page's box (`box`), the sign-in page (`login`), an assistant's connector (`connector`), an invitation's link (`invitation`), or a letter or a text to the platform (`email`, `text`). The rest is what their browser's arrival held (arrival.ts `Came`), where there was one: `page`, the home page they opened last (variant.ts); `said`, the tags and click ids of the link that brought them, read whole; `campaign`, the funnel's name for those tags (arrival.ts `campaign`), kept apart to filter and group on; `app`, the app whose badge they followed. Beside them, `assistant` is the name the connector's client registered under, its own choice, and `inviter` who sent the invitation. Somebody invited by another's code (`referral`) is that entity's to say.

visitor_build.$comment: When the home page's box opened this space for a newcomer (newcomer.ts `oneBuild`). It stays once they keep it, so the platform admin's Visitor builds page (admin.ts) says who kept each build after the newcomer's own row is gone.

preview.$comment: A site somebody else may own, rebuilt here from its web address (newcomer.ts `previewing`). On a space: the box was given that address `at`, and the apps born here for KEEPING after are previews of it. On an app: it is one, private, marked on its pages and never indexed, until a domain of that site is verified on its space (domains.ts `refresh`), which takes the mark off both rows.

source.$comment: What its dollars bought (meter.ts `SOURCES`), kept by the day in the space's `trend.sources`.

at.$comment: When its dollars were spent, where before the write: a settlement correcting a hold lands on the day the hold was made.

spend.$comment: What a space just spent on its month: a letter, a model call, a voice's lease, an app's text, container seconds. The directory adds it to the `meter` inside the write's own transaction (meter.ts `spend`), so two spends at once both count, and takes it off again: it is never kept. A `held` spend is a model call or a voice's lease holding its most before it starts (model-spend.ts `reserved`), and the write is refused when it does not fit what is left of the month's budget. A `refunded` one is the platform owner's correction (budget.ts), `why` it was refunded, journaled with who wrote it since the meter is not. A `bought` one is a block of credit paid for, added to the space's `credit` (billing.ts `credited`). Stamped, all three, for the reason the budget is.

credit_block.$comment: One block of credit paid for (billing.ts `credited`), named by the checkout that sold it, so a payment told twice is credited once: the row is written only where none is, in the write whose `spend{bought}` adds the block to the space's `credit`. Stamped, for the reason the budget is.

signed_in.$comment: When this person last got in, and how (signin.ts `stamped`, T-34351). One row, so it holds the last way in rather than a trail — which is the question a standing sign-in link raises: has anybody used it at all — and `first`, when they first got in, written once by that first sign-in, which is the funnel's sign-up (T-149011). Not `kind`: it is a mark a person wears, never a thing of its own.

built.description: A Workers Build the kernel started through main's deploy hook, and the commit it rebuilds.
built.$comment: A build of yaks.app the kernel asked main's deploy hook for, and the commit it asked for: the build's own record names none (builds.ts).
